description:
You are a deployment engineer responsible for rolling out updates to the application logs. There are two log files located in the directory /home/user/logs/: app.log and error.log. Your task is to write a shell command that will append the deployment timestamp to both log files. The timestamp must be in the UTC format "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS UTC". 

For both files, the appended line should be: 
Deployment completed: <timestamp>

Make sure both app.log and error.log contain this exact line at the end of the file. This must be the only change made to the files; do not modify any other contents in them. The automated test will verify that both files end with this precise line, using the timestamp at the time of execution. 

Do not create new files; only append to /home/user/logs/app.log and /home/user/logs/error.log.
truth:
Prior to the task, the following files exist:

/home/user/logs/app.log with arbitrary previous contents:

/home/user/logs/error.log with arbitrary previous contents:

None
...

After completing the task, the last line of both files must be:
Deployment completed: 2024-06-26 15:30:45 UTC

(replace "2024-06-26 15:30:45 UTC" with the current UTC timestamp in the format "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS UTC" at execution)

Both /home/user/logs/app.log and /home/user/logs/error.log must only be appended, preserving all previous contents, with the new deployment line as the very last line.
